item.title: Trump Names Intelligence Chief Clayton as AI Czar, to Head Task Force
item.description: Trump, who has pushed to rename artificial intelligence as “super intelligence,” said Clayton would head the newly created Super Intelligence Force (SIF), overseeing the government’s engagement with consumers, religious groups, AI companies and other stakeholders. In addition to Clayton, the task force’s leaders will include Federal Trade Commission Chairman Andrew Ferguson, Pentagon Chief Technology Officer Emil Michael and Office of Personnel Management Director Scott Kupor, Trump wrote. US President Donald Trump said on Sunday he had named Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton the administration’s AI czar, tasking him with coordinating the federal government’s efforts to maintain US leadership in the technology.

item.title: Crunchbase Data Shows AI’s Most Active Startups Are Becoming Serial Acquirers
item.description: Some of the AI industry’s fastest-growing startups are becoming serial acquirers, buying smaller companies to fill product gaps, enter new markets and bring specialized teams in-house, a review of Crunchbase data shows. The question we always ask is: does this deal get us somewhere faster than we’d get there ourselves?” Some of the AI acquirers have returned to the dealmaking table more than once in recent years, Crunchbase data shows. 29, according to Crunchbase data — 14% more than in all of 2025.

item.title: Third-party capital more than just complementary capacity for Hannover Re: Althoff
item.description: Sven Althoff, Member of the Executive Board for Property & Casualty at Hannover Re, has said that third-party capital is certainly part of the reinsurer’s strategy, describing it as more than just complementary capacity, whilst also adding that it is creating opportunities for Hannover Re. During the webinar, Althoff was asked whether he sees third-party capital as competition, complementary capacity or an integral part of Hannover Re’s own capital strategy. Althoff outlined that while third-party capital is a competitor in some respects, Hannover Re sees it as being more of a partner and opportunity to grow its business further.

item.title: Economics of ILS and appetites of investors change with the reinsurance cycle: Moody’s
item.description: In a recent report, Moody’s Ratings highlights how the economics of catastrophe bonds and insurance-linked securities change over time, driven by the softening global reinsurance market cycle. Moody’s Ratings recent report on the insurance-linked securities market, releases just in advance of the Monte Carlo Rendez-vous event, shows how cyclicality in reinsurance has played across into catastrophe bond pricing, with the agency saying this has changed the economics and as a result investor appetites are evolving. The last five years has shown the cycle remains fully in-force across reinsurance and whatever the unlock may be, that can make risk and capital flow more freely along the market chain and so moderate pricing cyclicality, has yet to be seen.

item.title: VisionFund teams with Global Parametrics on two-peril Amazon Basin parametric insurance
item.description: VisionFund, the financial inclusion arm of World Vision, working alongside with Global Parametrics and co-financed by the InsuResilience Solutions Fund, will design a two-peril parametric meso-insurance product for World Vision offices in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia and Peru, as part of the wider Amazon Basin Initiative. The firm’s explained that that the integrated approach builds on VisionFund’s experience in inclusive insurance, including more than eight years of climate meso-insurance, along with World Vision’s extensive disaster preparedness and response experience in the Amazon Basin region and globally. Solène Favre, VisionFund Global Director, Inclusive Insurance, commented: “This approach moves disaster and climate response from reactive fundraising towards pre-arranged, predictable protection.

item.title: Santam Syndicate 1918 appoints Sam Geddes as Active Underwriter
item.description: Santam Syndicate 1918, part of Santam Group, Africa’s non-life insurer, has announced that Sam Geddes will assume the responsibilities of Active Underwriter. According to Santam Syndicate 1918, the appointment comes as the Syndicate continues to develop its underwriting platform and expand its presence in the Lloyd’s market. item.title: Aon reinforces commitment to Taiwan with new corporate office in Taipei
item.description: Aon, a global professional services firm specialising in risk, insurance, retirement and health solutions, has announced the relocation of its Taiwan corporate office at Fubon A25 in Xinyi District. It reflects our long-term commitment to Taiwan and creates an environment for our colleagues to collaborate, innovate and succeed, while continuing to deliver the insights and solutions our clients need in an increasingly complex risk environment.” Designed to support a modern working style, the new office includes dedicated spaces for focused work, collaboration and team meetings, fostering greater connectivity among colleagues within a custom-built environment. Lee Huang Ng, Chairperson and CEO of Taiwan, Aon, commented: “The opening of our new office in Xinyi District is an important milestone for our Taiwan business.

item.title: L’Oreal Explores Unloading Chemical-Related Liabilities, WSJ Reports
item.description: L’Oreal has engaged restructuring advisers to explore options for rising US legal liabilities linked to its use of talc and other chemical ingredients in some of its cosmetic products, the Wall Street Journal reported on Monday. The Journal said L’Oreal is considering moving tort liabilities into a separate corporate entity to unload them through a sale to an outside investor, allowing the company to separate its exposure from its operating businesses. As an option to address the claims outside Chapter 11, L’Oreal’s advisers are exploring a sale similar to Honeywell’s divestiture last year of certain asbestos liabilities to corporate liability acquisition platform Delticus, the Journal said.

item.title: Rubio Asks Russia to Share More Information About Plague Death
item.description: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Tuesday that Russia should share more information about the death of a plague laboratory worker who died last week, an incident which he said Washington was watching “very closely.” “I think it’s incumbent upon Russia to obviously share more information with the world,” Rubio told reporters in Iceland. Rubio said the US has “measures” available to help Russia if the situation turns out to be more serious than has so far been acknowledged, but needed to know more before it could step in. (Editor’s note: The plague research institute is located in Irkutsk, a city in the Siberian Federal District of eastern Russia.) Russian authorities have said the situation is under control.

item.title: New York Declares US Measles Disaster Emergency
item.description: New York Governor Kathy Hochul declared a statewide disaster emergency on Monday over a measles outbreak, the first such declaration by a U.S. New York has reported 108 measles cases this year through October 3, including 92 since July 15 in under-immunized rural communities across 18 counties, well above typical annual levels, according to the executive order. The state also expanded the pool of health professionals allowed to administer measles-mumps-rubella (MMR) vaccines as cases rise in rural communities.

item.title: Canopius replaces QBE as Castle Insurance underwriter
item.description: Castle Insurance, part of Australia’s Sure Insurance , has named Canopius as its new underwriter, replacing QBE Insurance Australia effective December 1, 2026. Castle offers home and contents insurance through brokers and has been operating for approximately 12 months. Sure Insurance Managing Director Bradley Heath said the partnership offers new growth opportunities for Castle, citing the companies’ shared focus on long-term partnerships and specialized risk selection.

item.title: Nettle raises $4.8 million
item.description: Nettle , an AI loss control platform for commercial insurers, has raised $4.8 million in seed funding led by MTech Capital, with participation from Project A, Sure Valley Ventures, Portfolio Ventures, and Ventures Together. The round brings its total funding to $6.8 million, following a $2 million pre-seed round in March 2025. Founded in 2024 by former McKinsey QuantumBlack colleagues Jack Miller and Katya Kinane, Nettle combines remote risk identification, guided inspections, evidence analysis, and report generation.

By combining Allianz’s insurance expertise with Saga’s deep customer understanding, we’ve created something that feels relevant, accessible and genuinely unique for this audience.” – Isabella Von Mesterhazy, Managing Director of Allianz Specialty.

item.title: México alista nuevas reglas para pagos digitales: industria las apoya, pero pide preservar incentivos
item.description: La industria respalda el impulso a la digitalización, pero pide que las nuevas normas preserven la neutralidad tecnológica y mantengan incentivos para seguir expandiendo la aceptación de pagos electrónicos. México emprenderá reformas regulatorias para ampliar la aceptación de pagos digitales, con el objetivo de reducir costos para los comercios, extender el uso de medios electrónicos en trámites y servicios públicos y fortalecer la interoperabilidad entre bancos, fintechs y procesadores. Los cambios normativos avanzan en dos frentes: un anteproyecto regulatorio que plantea ajustes a los costos de procesamiento y a las cuotas de intercambio en operaciones con tarjeta, y la iniciativa de Ley de Economía Digital , que busca ampliar la aceptación de pagos electrónicos en los tres niveles de gobierno y facilitar una mayor adopción de códigos QR.

item.title: F&G files trademark application for “F&G FastPath”
item.description: F&G has filed a trademark application for “F&G FastPath” covering life insurance and annuity services. Filed on October 1, 2026, the application lists annuity underwriting, life insurance underwriting, issuance and administration of annuities, and issuance of life insurance. The application has not yet been assigned to an examiner.

item.title: Blitzy launches review tool for AI-generated code
item.description: Blitzy , an autonomous software development platform backed by Erie Strategic Ventures, Liberty Mutual Strategic Ventures, and New York Life Ventures, has launched PR Review, a feature designed to help engineering teams understand and review AI-generated code faster. The launch addresses a growing bottleneck as AI agents generate code faster than engineers can review it. Blitzy’s process allows engineers to approve the proposed scope and approach before code generation, with automated tests, builds, benchmarks, and static analysis incorporated into development.

item.title: SIAA acquires Canopy Specialty Insurance

item.title: Sedgwick: Property Claims Face Delays, Are Growing More Complex
item.description: Despite the promise of artificial intelligence and other technology to improve and speed the insurance process, property claims face delays and growing complexity, according to a new report that also shows claims costs are under pressure. Several factors are putting pressure on property claim timelines, including labor shortages, equipment delays and increasingly complex losses, according to Sedgwick’s annual Loss Adjusting Insights report . “It’s just what we call the silver tsunami and that’s really just kind of a moment, where we’re getting a little bit of a brain drain and claims are becoming more and more complex, just because of the intricacies of the policies the way they’re underwritten,” McCallum said.

item.title: Crunchbase Data: Q3 2026 Posted A Record Count Of Billion-Dollar Rounds As The Global AI Race Heats Up
item.description: Global venture funding totaled $159 billion in Q3 2026 with close to 6,000 startups funded, Crunchbase data shows. Funding to private companies has skyrocketed this year, totaling $679 billion in venture funding globally in Q1 through Q3 2026, per Crunchbase data. A notable shift in 2026 has been the number of startups that have raised billion-dollar-plus rounds.

item.title: Eaton Vance mutual fund ILS holdings hit $777m, new Swiss Re and Jaffa Capital investments
item.description: Holdings in insurance-linked securities fund structures and reinsurance sidecars made by Eaton Vance through three of its mutual funds have risen in value to approximately $777 million over the last quarter of record, as the asset manager allocated more to its investment in the Swiss Re Core Nat Cat Fund and added a new allocation to the Jaffa Capital Fund. Now, the total value of ILS investments across the three Eaton Vance mutual fund strategies we can track has increased by a further 14% to almost $777 million, while we can see from its filings that an additional investment seems to have been made into Swiss Re’s Core Nat Cat Fund strategy, plus a brand new investment has been made into the Jaffa Capital Fund. We last reported on the ILS allocations made by three of the Eaton Vance, part of Morgan Stanley Investment Management, mutual fund strategies back in July.

item.title: UCITS cat bond funds average 6.67% return YTD, fourth highest annual figure on record: Plenum Index
item.description: Specialist catastrophe bond and insurance bond investment manager Plenum Investment’s Index has a history back to 2011 and this year is now on-track to be at the least the fourth best annual return for UCITS cat bond funds. Catastrophe bond funds structured as UCITS investment strategies are now averaging a 6.67% return for the year to September 25th 2026, which is already the fourth best year on record for the Plenum CAT Bond UCITS Fund Indices . The latest data from the Plenum Index is for the period August 28th through September 25th 2026, for which time-frame the average return of the UCITS catastrophe bond funds reached 1.23%.

item.title: PICC P&C appears to have returned for its second Great Wall Re catastrophe bond
item.description: Chinese domestic insurer PICC Property and Casualty Company Limited seems to have returned to sponsor its second catastrophe bond using its Hong Kong domiciled special purpose insurer Great Wall Re Limited, as information of a new tranche of notes has appeared albeit with very limited details available at this time. That first Great Wall Re cat bond utilised an indemnity trigger and provided its earthquake reinsurance protection to PICC P&C on a per-occurrence basis and the company called the inaugural cat bond it had sponsored “an important measure to build a dual-pillar risk diversification system of reinsurance and insurance risk securitization.” Now, it appears as if PICC P&C has returned to the cat bond market, with a new tranche of notes issued by Great Wall Re Limited and being featured on certain securities market data services. In that debut instance, PICC P&C sponsored a $32.5 million Great Wall Re Limited cat bond deal, with the notes providing it with a roughly three-year source of fully-collateralized earthquake reinsurance in China, funded by investors from the insurance-linked securities (ILS) market.

item.title: Chaucer and Indemni new US Cargo proposition to target strategic theft
item.description: Global specialty reinsurance and insurance group Chaucer has partnered with I ndemni, a technology-led cargo risk specialist and newly approved Lloyd’s coverholder, to launch a specialist US cargo insurance proposition designed to target strategic theft. Adding: “By incorporating those controls into the proposition itself, we can take a more informed approach to risk selection while providing insurance protection designed around the way these losses actually occur, and create a stronger framework for preventing, identifying and responding to the strategic theft threat.” This product rollout marks a key milestone in their ongoing collaboration, building upon Chaucer’s earlier support of Indemni’s successful Lloyd’s coverholder application. The new offering will provide cover for US land transit risks across single-trip transit, annual contingent cargo and standalone strategic theft.

item.title: Union Pacific Railroad Fined $304K for Firing Employee During Severe Weather
item.description: Department of Labor Occupational Safety and Health Administration whistleblower investigation has concluded that Union Pacific Railroad Co. Within minutes of the stand-down, Union Pacific removed the employee from service and was later charged with insubordination. On June 10, 2026, OSHA ordered Union Pacific to remove from the employee’s employment records any reference of the incident, and pay back wages, lost benefits, compensatory and punitive damages totaling at least $304,869, and attorney’s fees.

item.title: AM Best Revises Outlook to Positive for Minnesota’s RAM Mutual Insurance
item.description: AM Best has revised the outlooks to positive from stable and affirmed the Financial Strength Rating of B++ (Good) and the Long-Term Issuer Credit Rating of “bbb+” (Good) of RAM Mutual Insurance Company (RAM) based in Esko, Minnesota. The outlook revisions to positive from stable reflect improved underwriting and overall operating results in each of the past two years and through the first half of 2026. The Credit Ratings (ratings) reflect RAM’s balance sheet strength, which AM Best assesses as very strong, as well as its marginal operating performance, limited business profile and appropriate enterprise risk management (ERM).

item.title: Branch restructures independent agency channel
item.description: Branch is restructuring its independent agency channel, affecting multiple employees, according to a LinkedIn post by JC Ibanez , a senior agency success manager at Branch. In response to Coverager’s inquiry, Branch said it is reorganizing its independent agency team to provide faster service and give agency partners more ways to grow their business. Branch plans to introduce tools in the coming months to help agents quote and bind more business.

item.title: Savvy opens insurance shopping to AI agents
item.description: Engine by Gen has updated its insurance marketplace, Savvy Insurance Solutions , to support AI agents shopping on consumers’ behalf, including assistants such as Muse and Instinct. The launch comes as insurance marketplaces consider how to handle automated shopping, with some restricting or blocking AI agents. When AI agents shop for insurance without using Savvy, people quickly lose control over their personal information as AI may share it with untold insurance websites, which leads to spam and risk of identity theft .

item.title: Prismic Life announces $5 billion reinsurance agreement with Prudential
item.description: Prismic Life Reinsurance announced an agreement with Prudential Financial to reinsure a portion of Prudential’s recently originated Japanese whole life policies. Under the terms of the agreement, Prismic will reinsure approximately $5 billion of reserves backing USD-denominated Japanese whole life insurance policies originated by Prudential’s Japanese affiliates. The transaction expands Prismic’s growing reinsurance platform and builds on the existing relationship between Prismic and Prudential, including in-force and new business flow transactions now covering more than $22 billion of USD-denominated liabilities.

item.title: US P/C Insurers See Fewer Ratings Downgrades in H1 2026 on Improved Performance
item.description: property/casualty insurance segment saw substantially fewer ratings downgrades with more ratings upgrades in the first half of 2026 — mostly related to either poor or improved operating performance, according to AM Best. There were about half as many downgrades in the first half of 2026 — or 3.8% of total rating actions, compared to 6.1% in the same period last year, said the ratings agency in a report titled “ Substantially Fewer Downgrades for US P/C Insurers in First Half of 2026 .” Upgrades increased to 8.2% of total rating actions in the first half of 2026, compared to 5.5% in H1 2025, the report continued. “Over half of downgrades were driven by poor operating performance, as some insurers have struggled to keep losses under control.
